periods.name: Incarnation & Birth
periods.subtitle: Matthew 1–2 · Luke 1–2 · John 1
periods.description: The Word becomes flesh. Angels announce Him, a virgin bears Him, shepherds and magi find Him, and a king tries to kill Him.

periods.name: The Hidden Years
periods.subtitle: Luke 2:40-52
periods.description: Nearly three decades pass in near silence. The one glimpse Scripture gives is a twelve-year-old in the temple, already about His Father's business.

events.title: The boy in the temple
events.summary: Twelve years old, missing for three days, found questioning the teachers. His first recorded words are about His Father's house.

periods.name: Baptism & Temptation
periods.subtitle: Matthew 3–4 · Mark 1 · Luke 3–4
periods.description: The Father speaks over Him at the Jordan, the Spirit drives Him into the wilderness, and He answers the tempter with Scripture alone.

events.title: The baptism of Jesus
events.summary: John protests that it should be the other way round. The heavens open and the Father speaks.

events.title: The temptation in the wilderness
events.summary: Forty days, three offers, three answers — every one of them a quotation from Deuteronomy.

periods.name: Early Ministry
periods.subtitle: John 1–4
periods.description: First disciples, first sign, first cleansing of the temple, and two conversations that define the gospel — with a ruler by night and a woman at noon.

events.title: What are you seeking?
events.summary: The first words He speaks in John's gospel.

events.title: Nathanael under the fig tree
events.summary: "Can anything good come out of Nazareth?" He answers the scepticism by describing where the man had been sitting.

events.title: Water into wine at Cana
events.summary: At a wedding running out of wine, He turns six stone jars of water into the best wine of the feast — the first of His signs.

events.title: Cleansing the temple
events.summary: A whip of cords, overturned tables, and a quotation about a house of prayer becoming a den of robbers.

events.title: Nicodemus, by night
events.summary: A member of the ruling council comes in the dark with a compliment and leaves with a riddle about birth.

events.title: You must be born again
events.summary: To a Pharisee who came at night, He says the kingdom is not entered by improvement but by birth.

events.title: The woman at the well
events.summary: Wrong nation, wrong gender, wrong hour, wrong history — and the longest recorded conversation He has with anyone.

events.title: Living water
events.summary: At a well at noon, to a woman with five husbands, He offers water that ends thirst permanently.

events.title: I who speak to you am He
events.summary: The first person He tells plainly that He is the Messiah is a Samaritan woman at a well.

events.title: Healing the official's son
events.summary: A royal official begs Him to come to Capernaum. Jesus heals from a day's journey away, and the father believes before he sees.

periods.name: The Galilean Ministry
periods.subtitle: Matthew 4–15 · Mark 1–7 · Luke 4–9
periods.description: The crowds swell. He preaches the Kingdom on a hillside, heals whoever comes, calms a sea, and feeds thousands from a boy's lunch.

events.title: The rejection at Nazareth
events.summary: He reads Isaiah in His hometown synagogue, says it is fulfilled today, and they try to throw Him off a cliff.

events.title: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
events.summary: The first thing He preaches, and the summary of everything after.

events.title: Calling the first disciples
events.summary: By the Sea of Galilee He interrupts four men mid-livelihood, and immediately they leave the nets.

events.title: Driving out an unclean spirit in Capernaum
events.summary: In the synagogue a demon names Him aloud. He silences it and casts it out, and the crowd realises His authority is not borrowed.

events.title: Healing Peter's mother-in-law
events.summary: He takes her hand and the fever leaves. She gets up and serves them — the first thing healing produces is service.

events.title: Healing everyone who came
events.summary: Whole evenings spent at a door, laying hands on each one — the gospels record it almost in passing.

events.title: The miraculous catch of fish
events.summary: After a fruitless night, Peter lets down the nets on His word and the catch nearly sinks two boats. Peter falls at His knees.

events.title: Cleansing a leper
events.summary: "If you are willing, you can make me clean." He reaches out and touches the untouchable before He says a word.

events.title: The paralytic lowered through the roof
events.summary: Four friends dig through a roof. He forgives the man's sins first — then heals him to prove He had the right to.

events.title: Calling Matthew from the tax booth
events.summary: He recruits a collaborator, then goes to dinner at his house with all his friends.

events.title: New Wine and Old Wineskins
events.summary: You cannot patch the new onto the old. What He brings will not fit inside what was there before.

events.title: Healing at the pool of Bethesda
events.summary: Thirty-eight years of waiting end with a question and a command. It happens on a Sabbath, and the trouble begins.

events.title: Do you want to be healed?
events.summary: Asked of a man who had been lying by the pool for thirty-eight years.

events.title: The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath
events.summary: Challenged over His disciples picking grain, He claims authority over the day itself.

events.title: Something greater than the temple is here
events.summary: Greater than the temple, greater than Jonah, greater than Solomon — three claims in one confrontation.

events.title: Healing the man with the withered hand
events.summary: They watch to see if He will heal on the Sabbath. He does it in the middle of the synagogue, grieved at their hard hearts.

events.title: The Beatitudes
events.summary: He opens the Sermon on the Mount by congratulating exactly the people nobody congratulates.

events.title: I came not to abolish the Law but to fulfil it
events.summary: He positions Himself not against the Scriptures but as their destination.

events.title: Salt and Light
events.summary: Two images for the same point: His followers are for the world, not withdrawn from it.

events.title: Let your light shine before others
events.summary: Visibility with a redirected credit line — so they see your works and glorify your Father.

events.title: On anger and reconciliation
events.summary: He traces murder back to contempt, and tells you to leave your gift at the altar and go make it right.

events.title: On lust and the heart
events.summary: The commandment reaches past the act to the look, and the remedy He prescribes is drastic.

events.title: On oaths and plain speech
events.summary: Do not swear at all. Let your yes be yes — integrity that needs no escalation.

events.title: On retaliation
events.summary: The other cheek, the second mile, the cloak as well — refusing to let an aggressor set the terms.

events.title: Give to the one who asks of you
events.summary: No means test, no assessment of deserving — an instruction that assumes you will sometimes be taken advantage of.

events.title: Love your enemies
events.summary: The command that has no natural constituency — and the one He grounds in the character of the Father.

events.title: On giving to the needy
events.summary: Give so quietly that your left hand does not know. The audience you play to is the reward you get.

events.title: Pray then like this
events.summary: The prayer He gave when asked how to pray — short, corporate, and addressed to a Father.

events.title: On fasting
events.summary: Wash your face and comb your hair. The point is not to be seen doing it.

events.title: Treasures in heaven and two masters
events.summary: Where your treasure is, your heart follows — and no one can serve God and money.

events.title: Which of you by being anxious can add an hour to his life?
events.summary: Part of a sustained argument that worry is not only painful but useless.

events.title: Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye?
events.summary: The question is not whether the speck is there. It is what is in your own eye while you look.

events.title: Ask, seek, knock
events.summary: Three imperatives in the present tense: keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking.

events.title: Do to others as you would have them do to you
events.summary: Stated positively rather than as a prohibition — and called the sum of the Law and the Prophets.

events.title: Enter by the narrow gate
events.summary: Two gates, two roads, two destinations — and the popular one is not the one He recommends.

events.title: A tree and its fruit
events.summary: False prophets are identified not by their claims but by what grows on them over time.

events.title: The Wise and Foolish Builders
events.summary: Two houses, one storm. The difference was invisible until the rain came — and it was the foundation.

events.title: Healing the centurion's servant
events.summary: A Roman officer says a word from a distance will do. Jesus marvels — He has not found such faith in Israel.

events.title: Raising the widow's son at Nain
events.summary: He meets a funeral procession, has compassion on the mother, stops the bier and gives her son back to her.

events.title: "Do not weep"
events.summary: He interrupts a funeral for a woman who has now lost both husband and only son, because He saw her.

events.title: Come to me, all who labour
events.summary: An invitation offering not the removal of a yoke but the exchange of one for an easier one.

events.title: Woe to Chorazin and Bethsaida
events.summary: He names the towns that saw the most and repented least, and compares them unfavourably to Sodom.

events.title: The woman who wept on His feet
events.summary: At a Pharisee's dinner, an uninvited woman with a bad reputation and an alabaster flask.

events.title: The Two Debtors
events.summary: Two debts cancelled, one ten times the other. "Which of them will love him more?"

events.title: The Beelzebul accusation
events.summary: Accused of casting out demons by the prince of demons, He points out that a divided kingdom cannot stand.

events.title: The demand for a sign
events.summary: They want proof. He sighs deeply and says no sign will be given except the sign of Jonah.

events.title: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
events.summary: Told His family is outside asking for Him, He redraws the family line around obedience.

events.title: The Sower
events.summary: One seed, four soils. The difference is never the seed — it is the ground it lands on.

events.title: The Lamp Under a Basket
events.summary: Nobody lights a lamp to hide it. Nothing is concealed that will not be brought into the open.

events.title: The Growing Seed
events.summary: The farmer sleeps and rises; the seed sprouts and grows, he knows not how. Growth is not his doing.

events.title: The Weeds Among the Wheat
events.summary: An enemy sows weeds in the night. The servants want to pull them; the owner says wait for the harvest.

events.title: The Mustard Seed
events.summary: The smallest of seeds becomes a tree the birds nest in. The Kingdom starts smaller than anyone expects.

events.title: The Leaven
events.summary: A little yeast hidden in three measures of flour works through all of it — invisibly, and completely.

events.title: The Hidden Treasure
events.summary: A man finds treasure in a field and sells everything he has for it — joyfully.

events.title: The Pearl of Great Price
events.summary: A merchant who knows pearls finds one worth more than all the rest, and liquidates his life to own it.

events.title: The Net
events.summary: A dragnet gathers fish of every kind. The sorting happens on the shore, not in the water.

events.title: Calming the storm
events.summary: Asleep in the stern through a squall. He rebukes the wind, then asks them why they were afraid.

events.title: Where is your faith?
events.summary: Not "do you have faith" but where it went when the water started coming in.

events.title: The Gerasene demoniac
events.summary: A man no chain could hold is left clothed and in his right mind. The town asks Jesus to leave.

events.title: The woman who touched His garment
events.summary: Twelve years of bleeding, and no doctor could help. She touches the fringe of His cloak in a crowd and He stops everything to find her.

events.title: Raising Jairus' daughter
events.summary: A synagogue ruler's daughter dies while Jesus is delayed. He tells him only to believe, then takes her hand: "Little girl, arise."

events.title: Healing two blind men
events.summary: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" He touches their eyes according to their faith.

events.title: Do you believe that I am able to do this?
events.summary: Asked of two blind men before He touches their eyes — the healing follows the answer.

events.title: Healing a mute demoniac
events.summary: The crowds marvel; the Pharisees say He casts out demons by the prince of demons. The same act, two verdicts.

events.title: Moved with compassion for the crowds
events.summary: He sees them harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd — and tells the disciples to pray for workers.

events.title: Go and preach: the kingdom is at hand
events.summary: He sends the Twelve out with His own authority and His own message — and tells them to go without provisions.

events.title: Sheep in the midst of wolves
events.summary: He promises the Twelve opposition, not success — courts, floggings, family betrayal — and the Spirit's words when they are on trial.

events.title: Do not fear those who kill the body
events.summary: Fear moves from men to God, and in the same breath the God who numbers every hair on their heads.

events.title: I did not come to bring peace, but a sword
events.summary: Loyalty to Him will divide households, and whoever will not take up the cross is not worthy of Him.

events.title: He who receives you receives Me
events.summary: His messengers carry Him with them: to welcome them is to welcome Him and the Father who sent Him, down to a cup of cold water.

events.title: Feeding the five thousand
events.summary: Five loaves, two fish, and twelve baskets left over — the only miracle all four gospels record.

events.title: How many loaves do you have?
events.summary: Before He multiplies anything He asks them to inventory what little they actually hold.

events.title: Walking on the water
events.summary: He comes to them in the fourth watch. Peter walks, then looks at the wind, then sinks — and is caught.

events.title: Many healed at Gennesaret
events.summary: They run through the whole region carrying the sick on mats and beg only to touch the fringe of His cloak. Everyone who touches it is made well.

events.title: The bread of life discourse
events.summary: The hardest sermon He preached, measured by results: many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.

events.title: I am the bread of life
events.summary: Said the day after He fed five thousand, to a crowd that came back wanting more bread.

events.title: The tradition of the elders
events.summary: Challenged about unwashed hands, He accuses them of using tradition to nullify the commandment of God.

events.title: The Syrophoenician woman's daughter
events.summary: A Gentile mother refuses to be turned away and answers Him from inside His own metaphor. He calls her faith great.

events.title: Healing a deaf and mute man
events.summary: He takes the man aside privately, sighs, and says "Ephphatha" — be opened.

events.title: Feeding the four thousand
events.summary: Three days without food in Gentile territory. "I have compassion on the crowd" — and He does it again.

events.title: The blind man at Bethsaida
events.summary: The only healing that comes in two stages — first men like trees walking, then everything clearly.

events.title: Do you not yet understand?
events.summary: Seven rapid-fire questions to disciples worried about bread, days after two mass feedings.

events.title: Beware the leaven of the Pharisees
events.summary: A small amount of hypocrisy, He warns, does to a life what yeast does to dough.

periods.name: The Turning Point
periods.subtitle: Matthew 16–18 · Mark 8–9 · Luke 9
periods.description: At Caesarea Philippi Peter names Him Messiah — and from that moment He begins to speak plainly about the cross.

events.title: Peter's confession at Caesarea Philippi
events.summary: Far north of Galilee, at the foot of a cliff full of pagan shrines, Peter says: You are the Christ.

events.title: The Son of Man must suffer
events.summary: From Caesarea Philippi onward He says it plainly and repeatedly — and they keep not hearing it.

events.title: Get behind me, Satan
events.summary: Minutes after Peter's great confession, Peter tries to talk Him out of the cross and is rebuked by name.

events.title: Take up your cross and follow me
events.summary: Said to people who had watched actual crucifixions. It was not a metaphor for inconvenience.

events.title: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world?
events.summary: A cost-benefit question about the only asset that cannot be replaced.

events.title: The Transfiguration
events.summary: On a high mountain His face shines like the sun. Moses and Elijah appear, and the Father speaks again: "Listen to Him."

events.title: The boy with an unclean spirit
events.summary: "I believe; help my unbelief!" A father's honest prayer at the foot of the mountain of transfiguration.

events.title: The coin in the fish's mouth
events.summary: To avoid giving offence over the temple tax, He sends Peter fishing for exactly the right coin.

events.title: Forgive seventy times seven
events.summary: Peter offers seven times, thinking himself generous. Jesus removes the ceiling entirely.

events.title: The Unforgiving Servant
events.summary: Forgiven an unpayable debt, he throttles a man over pocket change. Forgiveness you keep is forgiveness you never took.

events.title: The Lost Sheep
events.summary: Ninety-nine left in the open country to go after one, and a party when it is carried home.

periods.name: The Road to Jerusalem
periods.subtitle: Luke 9:51–19:27 · John 7–11
periods.description: He sets His face toward Jerusalem. Most of the parables belong to this stretch, told to crowds who do not yet know where the road ends.

events.title: On forgiving before you pray
events.summary: Whenever you stand praying, forgive — He ties the vertical and the horizontal together and will not untie them.

events.title: What is written in the Law? How do you read it?
events.summary: A lawyer tests Him with a question. He answers with two questions and lets the man convict himself.

events.title: The Good Samaritan
events.summary: Asked to define "neighbour," He tells a story that redefines the question — and makes the hero the wrong nationality.

events.title: Which of these three proved to be a neighbour?
events.summary: The lawyer asked who his neighbour was. Jesus makes him answer who acted like one.

events.title: Mary and Martha
events.summary: One sister is serving, one is sitting. He defends the one who is not being useful.

events.title: The Friend at Midnight
events.summary: A neighbour gets up not out of friendship but because of shameless persistence. So keep asking.

events.title: The Rich Fool
events.summary: A bumper crop, bigger barns, and a comfortable retirement plan. "This night your soul is required of you."

events.title: The Watchful Servants
events.summary: Servants waiting up for a master returning from a wedding. Blessed are the ones he finds awake.

events.title: The Faithful and Wise Steward
events.summary: Put in charge while the master is away. To whom much is given, much will be required.

events.title: The Barren Fig Tree
events.summary: Three fruitless years and an owner ready to cut it down. The gardener asks for one more year.

events.title: The woman bent double for eighteen years
events.summary: He calls her over on a Sabbath and straightens her. The synagogue ruler is indignant; the crowd rejoices.

events.title: Healing a man with dropsy
events.summary: At a Pharisee's table, on a Sabbath, He asks whether it is lawful to heal — and no one will answer.

events.title: The Great Banquet
events.summary: Every invited guest has an excuse, so the host fills his house from the streets and the hedgerows.

events.title: On the cost of discipleship
events.summary: Great crowds are following Him, so He turns and tells them exactly what it will take.

events.title: The Tower and the King Going to War
events.summary: Count the cost before you start building, or going to battle. Discipleship is not an impulse purchase.

events.title: The Lost Coin
events.summary: A woman sweeps the whole house for one coin, and calls in the neighbours when she finds it.

events.title: The Prodigal Son
events.summary: A son who wanted his father dead, a father who ran to meet him, and an older brother who would not come in.

events.title: The Shrewd Manager
events.summary: A dishonest steward buys himself a future. Use worldly wealth the way he used his last week of access.

events.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
events.summary: A beggar at the gate and a man in purple. The gulf that was invisible in life turns out to be fixed.

events.title: The Unworthy Servants
events.summary: When you have done everything commanded, say: we are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.

events.title: Cleansing ten lepers
events.summary: Ten are healed on the way. One comes back — and he is a Samaritan.

events.title: Were not ten cleansed? Where are the nine?
events.summary: Ten lepers healed, one returned. The question is about gratitude, and it is left open.

events.title: The Persistent Widow
events.summary: She wears down an unjust judge. If he relents, how much more will a just Father hear?

events.title: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
events.summary: Two men pray. One lists his virtues; one will not lift his eyes. Only one goes home justified.

events.title: On divorce and marriage
events.summary: Asked which grounds are permissible, He goes back past Moses to Genesis and the intention behind it.

events.title: Blessing the children
events.summary: Parents bring children, disciples turn them away, and He takes them in His arms.

events.title: The rich young ruler
events.summary: The only person in the gospels who is invited to follow Him and refuses. Mark notes that Jesus loved him.

events.title: The Workers in the Vineyard
events.summary: Everyone gets a denarius, whether they worked twelve hours or one. Grace looks like unfairness from the front of the line.

events.title: On greatness and servanthood
events.summary: Two disciples ask for the best seats. He redefines the ranking: whoever would be great must serve.

events.title: What do you want me to do for you?
events.summary: Asked of a blind beggar — and, in the same week, of two disciples angling for thrones.

events.title: Blind Bartimaeus
events.summary: Shouted down by the crowd, he shouts louder. Jesus stops the procession and asks what he wants.

events.title: Zacchaeus in the sycamore tree
events.summary: He invites Himself to lunch at the house of the most hated man in Jericho, and the man gives half his goods away.

events.title: The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost
events.summary: His own summary of why He came, said in the house of a tax collector everyone was grumbling about.

events.title: The Ten Minas
events.summary: A nobleman leaves to receive a kingdom, and his citizens send word that they will not have him reign.

events.title: Why do you seek to kill me?
events.summary: Asked openly in the temple courts, to a crowd that denied they were doing any such thing.

events.title: The woman caught in adultery
events.summary: He writes in the dust, disarms a mob with one sentence, and is the only one left with standing to condemn her — and doesn't.

events.title: Go, and from now on sin no more
events.summary: Said after every accuser had walked away — neither condemnation nor permission.

events.title: I am the light of the world
events.summary: Spoken in the temple treasury, during a feast lit by enormous lampstands.

events.title: Before Abraham was, I AM
events.summary: The claim that made them pick up stones — He took the divine name for Himself.

events.title: "If God were your Father…"
events.summary: The sharpest exchange in the gospels, over descent from Abraham and who is actually doing whose works.

events.title: The man born blind
events.summary: Mud, a wash in Siloam, and an interrogation. "One thing I know: I was blind, now I see."

events.title: Do you believe in the Son of Man?
events.summary: He goes looking for the man born blind after the synagogue throws him out.

events.title: The Good Shepherd and the Sheepfold
events.summary: The sheep know the shepherd's voice. The hired hand runs; the shepherd lays down his life.

events.title: I came that they may have life abundantly
events.summary: Set against the thief who comes only to steal, kill and destroy.

events.title: I am the door of the sheep
events.summary: Not one way among several into the fold — the way in.

events.title: I am the good shepherd
events.summary: The claim He defines by what it costs: the shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

events.title: The Good Shepherd discourse
events.summary: Sheep, shepherd, hired hand, thief, and one flock — an extended claim about who He is and what He will do.

events.title: I and the Father are one
events.summary: At the Feast of Dedication, pressed to say plainly whether He is the Christ.

events.title: Raising Lazarus
events.summary: Four days in the tomb. He weeps at the grave of a friend He is about to raise, and calls him out by name.

events.title: Jesus wept
events.summary: He knew He was about to raise Lazarus. He cried anyway, and the shortest verse in the Bible records it.

events.title: The plot to kill Him
events.summary: Raising Lazarus is what finally decides them. The council reasons that it is expedient for one man to die for the people — and from that day they plan His death.

events.title: I am the resurrection and the life
events.summary: Said to Martha outside a tomb, four days too late — and then proved.

periods.name: Passion Week
periods.subtitle: Matthew 21–26 · Mark 11–14 · Luke 19–22 · John 12–17
periods.description: From the colt on Palm Sunday to the bread and cup in the upper room — seven days that the gospels slow almost to a standstill.

events.title: Mary of Bethany anoints Him for burial
events.summary: A year's wages poured out in a room that smelled of it afterwards, six days before the Passover.

events.title: The triumphal entry
events.summary: He arranges His own arrival on a borrowed colt, deliberately fulfilling Zechariah in front of everyone.

events.title: Weeping over Jerusalem
events.summary: In the middle of a celebration, He looks at the city and grieves what it does not know.

events.title: Withering the fig tree
events.summary: A tree in full leaf with no fruit, cursed on the way into Jerusalem — an acted parable about the temple.

events.title: By what authority are you doing these things?
events.summary: He answers a question with a question about John's baptism, and they refuse to answer it.

events.title: The Two Sons
events.summary: One says no and goes; one says yes and doesn't. Which one did the will of his father?

events.title: The Wicked Tenants
events.summary: Servant after servant is beaten, then the son is killed. The chief priests knew exactly who He meant.

events.title: The Wedding Feast
events.summary: The invited will not come, so the hall is filled from the highways — and one guest is still turned out.

events.title: The question about paying taxes
events.summary: Pharisees and Herodians — natural enemies — cooperate to trap Him, and He escapes with a coin.

events.title: The Sadducees' riddle
events.summary: Seven brothers, one wife, and a trap. He says God is the God of the living, not the dead.

events.title: Love God, love your neighbour
events.summary: Asked to rank 613 commandments, He gives two — and says everything else hangs on them.

events.title: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees
events.summary: Seven woes delivered in the temple courts — whitewashed tombs, strained gnats, swallowed camels.

events.title: The widow's two small coins
events.summary: He sits opposite the treasury and watches. She put in more than all of them, because she put in everything.

events.title: The Greeks who wished to see Jesus
events.summary: Outsiders ask for Him, and He answers that the hour has come — a grain of wheat must fall into the earth.

events.title: The Olivet Discourse
events.summary: Sitting opposite the temple He has just left, He describes its fall and His return, and tells them to keep watch.

events.title: The Fig Tree in Leaf
events.summary: When the branch is tender you know summer is near. Read the season you are living in.

events.title: Stay awake — you do not know the day
events.summary: The practical conclusion of the Olivet Discourse: not prediction, but readiness.

events.title: The Ten Virgins
events.summary: Five brought extra oil, five didn't. The bridegroom was delayed, and readiness could not be borrowed at midnight.

events.title: The Talents
events.summary: Two servants trade and double; one buries his in the ground and calls the master hard.

events.title: The Sheep and the Goats
events.summary: The nations are divided over meals given, clothes provided, prisons visited. "You did it to me."

events.title: On judgment and eternal accountability
events.summary: The hardest strand of His teaching: a reckoning is coming, and it is not a metaphor He softens.

events.title: The Last Supper
events.summary: A Passover meal in a borrowed room, a betrayal announced, and bread and wine given a new meaning.

events.title: Washing the disciples' feet
events.summary: Knowing the Father had given all things into His hands, He took a towel — including for the man about to betray Him.

events.title: Love one another as I have loved you
events.summary: Given the night before the cross, with the standard of comparison about to be demonstrated.

events.title: Let not your hearts be troubled
events.summary: Said hours before His arrest, to people about to lose everything they had built their lives around.

events.title: I am the way, the truth, and the life
events.summary: Thomas asks how they can know the way. The answer is not a map but a person.

events.title: Whoever has seen me has seen the Father
events.summary: Philip asks to be shown the Father. Jesus answers that he has been looking at Him for three years.

events.title: On the Helper who is coming
events.summary: It is to their advantage that He goes away, because then the Spirit of truth will come.

events.title: I am the true vine
events.summary: On the last night, the image He leaves them with is dependence, not effort.

events.title: Abide in me
events.summary: The one command in the vineyard discourse, and everything else is said to follow from it.

events.title: The Vine and the Branches
events.summary: Fruit is not produced by effort but by connection. "Apart from me you can do nothing."

events.title: The Upper Room Discourse
events.summary: Four chapters of last words: a place prepared, a Helper promised, a vine, and peace not as the world gives.

events.title: The High Priestly Prayer
events.summary: He prays aloud for Himself, for the eleven, and for everyone who would ever believe through their word.

periods.name: The Cross
periods.subtitle: Matthew 26–27 · Mark 14–15 · Luke 22–23 · John 18–19
periods.description: Betrayal, trial, and crucifixion. He answers almost nothing, forgives almost everyone, and finishes what He came to do.

events.title: Gethsemane
events.summary: "Not as I will, but as you will." He asks three times for the cup to pass, and goes anyway.

events.title: Whom are you seeking?
events.summary: Asked of an armed detachment in a garden. He walks toward them, not away.

events.title: Healing the servant's severed ear
events.summary: His last miracle before the cross repairs the damage done by a disciple defending Him.

events.title: The trial before the Sanhedrin
events.summary: Contradictory witnesses, a silent defendant, and one question He finally answers.

events.title: Jesus before Pilate
events.summary: A governor who can find no guilt in Him, a crowd that will not relent, and a question left hanging: what is truth?

events.title: My kingdom is not of this world
events.summary: Standing before Rome's governor, He concedes He is a king — of a kingdom Rome has no category for.

events.title: Father, forgive them
events.summary: His first recorded words from the cross are an intercession for the people driving in the nails.

events.title: The thief on the cross
events.summary: A dying criminal makes the simplest request in the gospels and gets an immediate promise.

events.title: Behold your mother
events.summary: Dying, He arranges His mother's care — a piece of family logistics handled from a cross.

events.title: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
events.summary: The hardest question in the gospels, and He is the one asking it — quoting Psalm 22 from the cross.

periods.name: Resurrection & Ascension
periods.subtitle: Matthew 28 · Mark 16 · Luke 24 · John 20–21
periods.description: An empty tomb, a gardener who says her name, a road to Emmaus, breakfast on a beach, and a commission that reaches every nation.

events.title: Mary Magdalene at the tomb
events.summary: The first witness of the resurrection is a woman who mistook Him for the gardener until He said her name.

events.title: Woman, why are you weeping?
events.summary: The risen Christ's first recorded words, asked of someone who thought He was the gardener.

events.title: The road to Emmaus
events.summary: Seven miles of Bible study with a stranger, and they only recognise Him when He breaks the bread.

events.title: Thomas and the wounds
events.summary: He returns a week later specifically for the one man who wasn't there, and offers him his hands.

events.title: The catch of 153 fish
events.summary: After the resurrection, another empty night and another word from the shore — and breakfast already cooking.

events.title: Restoring Peter on the beach
events.summary: Three denials by a charcoal fire, three questions by another charcoal fire.

events.title: Do you love me?
events.summary: Asked three times on a beach, once for each denial, and answered with a commission each time.

events.title: Feed my sheep
events.summary: Peter's restoration is not a pardon and a discharge — it is a pardon and a job.

events.title: Go and make disciples of all nations
events.summary: The last command, given on a mountain in Galilee to eleven men, some of whom still doubted.

events.title: All authority has been given to me
events.summary: The claim that grounds the Great Commission — the sending rests on the authority.

events.title: The Ascension
events.summary: He blesses them, and while blessing them is carried up — with a promise about how He will return.
